content: WikiDoc is a comprehensive online medical textbook supported by a diverse group of contributors, including students, physicians, and researchers. The New Pages project has been designed to assist all registered contributors, whether working onsite or remotely, in creating new pages in a streamlined manner. This approach ensures that the consistency and structure of the pages are maintained. The creation of a new page is a fundamental step that editors must understand when initiating their topics. To create a new page, there is a clear need for user-friendly guidelines tailored to the specific requirements of different projects. These guidelines should be consolidated and made easily accessible to all editors in a single, organized collection. The WikiDoc chief editor, along with other editors and scholars, has been actively working under the New Pages project to develop standardized guidelines. These guidelines are specifically designed for various topics and projects, such as new diseases, board review, crowd diagnosis, critical pathways, clinical guidelines, microchapters, disease prevalence, the resident survival guide, WikiDoc in other languages, and WikiPatient. The team continuously collaborates to update and refine these guidelines, ensuring they remain an efficient and user-friendly resource. WikiDoc encourages medical students, interns, residents, attending physicians, hospitalists, specialist doctors, researchers, nurses, physician assistants, and nurse practitioners to actively participate in the New Pages project. By contributing to this initiative, they can help enhance the quality and depth of the pages, ensuring the platform continues to thrive as a valuable medical resource.
